## Plant breeding {.custom1}

**Traditionally**, selection is based on the phenotype, but... 

$$
P = G + E + G \times E
$$

```{r fig.height=4}
library(tidyverse)
g_main <- rnorm(50, mean = 0, sd = 1) 
g_main <- rep(g_main, times = 30)

GE_int <- matrix(rnorm(50*30, mean = 0, sd = 2), ncol = 30)
ge_int <- c(GE_int) 
gv <- g_main + ge_int

e_main <- rnorm(30, mean = 0, sd = 4) 
e_main <- rep(e_main, each = 50)

dat = data.frame(
  G = g_main, 
  GE = ge_int, 
  E = e_main
)

dat$P = dat$G + dat$E + dat$GE

ggplot(data = dat |> pivot_longer(G:P) |> 
         mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("P","G", "E", "GE"))), aes(x = value, fill = name)) +
  facet_wrap(.~name, nrow = 1) + 
  geom_density()+
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title = element_blank(), text = element_text(size = 16))

```

## Genetic markers {.custom1}

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=7, fig.align='center'}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggsci)

nc = c("A", "T", "G", "C")
dat = expand.grid(nc, nc)
dat$fil = ifelse(dat$Var1 == dat$Var2, NA, 1)
aa = matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = 4, dimnames = list(nc, nc))

aa[upper.tri(aa)] = 1
as.data.frame(aa) |> rownames_to_column("x") |> pivot_longer(A:C) |> 
  mutate(fil = ifelse(is.na(value),NA,paste0(x, name))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(x, levels = nc), y = factor(name, levels = nc), 
             fill = fil)) + 
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = fil), fontface = "bold", color = "white", size = 10) +
  scale_fill_aaas() + 
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = 'none', axis.title = element_blank(),
                          text = element_text(size = 25), axis.text = element_blank(),
                          panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r fig.height=4}

gv <- g_main + ge_int
```

## Marker-assisted selection {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   Marker in [linkage disequilibrium]{.blue} with the causal genes
    -   Indirect selection
-   Higher selection intensity
-   Less time required for obtaining improved germplasm
-   Selection for traits that are hard to measure
-   Assistance in plant breeding routine procedures (backcrossing, gene pyramiding, ...)

:::

## Marker-assisted selection? {.custom1}

::: {style="font-size: 92%;"}

> "*Obviously, [the phenotype of interest needs to be unequivocally associated with the genomic region]{.underline} (i.e. the trait ↔ QTL correlation), determination of which is the focus of QTL mapping algorithms. However, even if a QTL explains 100% of the phenotypic variance for a trait of interest in a gene pool, [the QTL still needs to be unequivocally associated with the marker used to impose selection for it]{.underline} (i.e. the QTL ↔ marker correlation). [If either of these correlations (trait ↔ QTL or QTL ↔ marker) is poor, the trait ↔ marker association will not reliably improve the phenotype of interest]{.underline}, and so breeders may not only lose confidence in the value of a particular locus, but potentially in marker-assisted selection itself as an effective method.*" 
> --- @cobb_back_2019

:::

## Genomic selection {.custom1}

::: incremental
::: {style="font-size: 100%;"}
-   Most economically important traits are influenced by many genes
-   It is hard (impossible) to identify them all
-   Next-Generation Sequencing: whole genome coverage
-   [Genomic approach]{.green}: use all information available
    
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.35em"}

The main differences between QTL mapping, genome-wide association studies and genomic selection are in the objectives (inference or prediction) and in the statistical methods used to model the genetic effects

:::

## Why does it work? {.custom1}

Linkage between marker and QTL

```{=html}
<div class="figure-with-source">

  </div>
</div>
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

$$
\bar{y}_i = \mu + \sum_{m=1}^p x_{im} \beta_m + \varepsilon_i
$$

-   $x_{ij} \to$ allele dosage of marker $j$ in genotype $i$

-   $\beta_j \to$ effect of marker $j$ 

. . .

::: {.callout-tip style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
If genotypes share marker alleles, and these markers are in **linkage disequilibrium** with important QTL, then one can predict the performance of unseen genotypes using marker information.
:::

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{=html}
<div class="figure-with-source">
  <img src="C:/Users/saulo/OneDrive/Palestras/Misc/wallace.png" style="width: 78%;" />
  <div class="figure-source">
    <a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30285496/" target="_blank">Wallace et al. (2018)</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

$$
\bar{y}_i = \mu + x_{i1}\beta_1 + x_{i2}\beta_2 + \dots + x_{ip}\beta_p + \varepsilon_i
$$

. . .

::: {.callout-caution style="font-size: 1.3em;"}

## In the multiple regression setting...

Each marker would have a **fixed** value referred to its contribution to the phenotype, depending on how linked are the marker and the QTL
:::

## How does it work? {.custom1}


```{r echo=TRUE}
set.seed(55)
dat = data.frame(
  geno = paste0("G", 1:5),
  y = rnorm(5, mean = 10, sd = 2)
)
dat = cbind(dat, matrix(
  rbinom(35, size = 2, prob = .5),
  ncol = 7,
  nrow = 5,
  dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("M", 1:7))
))
dat
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4 + M5 + M6 + M7, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## Population types {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   **Training population**: used to estimate the model's parameters
    -   Both phenotyped and genotyped
-   **Testing population**: used to evaluate the model's predictive ability
    -   Both phenotyped and genotyped
-   **Breeding population**: where the model will be applied
    -   Only genotyped

:::

## Model evaluation {.custom1}

-   Predictive ability (PA): $\operatorname{Cor}\left(\bar{y},\hat{y}\right)$

. . .

-   Prediction accuracy (ACC): $\frac{\operatorname{Cor}\left(\bar{y},\hat{y}\right)}{\sqrt{h^2}}$

. . .

```{=html}
<div class="figure-with-source">
  <img src="C:/Users/saulo/OneDrive/Palestras/Misc//salva.png" style="width: 90%;" />
  <div class="figure-source">
    <a href="" target="_blank">Salvador Gezan</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

. . .

-   Root of mean squared prediction error: $\sqrt{\frac{1}{V}\sum^n_{i=1}(\bar{y}_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}$

## Concluding remarks {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   Genomic selection has high potential to increase plant breeding efficiency
    -   Increase selection intensity, decrease costs and generation interval
-   Inserting genomic selection into a breeding pipeline is not an easy task
    -   Which stage? 
    -   How to build a proper training population? 
    -   How to perform the selection and control the inbreeding? 
    -   How to deal with phenotypic and genomic data?
    
:::

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = extract.gt(x = vcf)
geno = geno[-grep(',', vcf@fix[,'ALT']),] # Remove multi-allelic mrks
vcf@fix = vcf@fix[-grep(',',vcf@fix[,'ALT']),]
geno = gsub('/', "", geno)
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
# Binding reference and alternative allele to marker matrix
geno = cbind(geno, vcf@fix[,c('REF', 'ALT')]) 
geno = apply(geno, 1, function(x){
  y = gsub('0', x['REF'], x)
  z = gsub('1', y['ALT'], y)
  z
})
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = geno[-which(rownames(geno) %in% c('REF', 'ALT')), ]
geno[grep('CA', geno)] = 'AC'
geno[grep('GA', geno)] = 'AG'
geno[grep('TA', geno)] = 'AT'
geno[grep('GC', geno)] = 'CG'
geno[grep('TC', geno)] = 'CT'
geno[grep('TG', geno)] = 'GT'
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

**Filtering step**

```{r echo=TRUE}
Freqsnps = apply(geno, 2, table)
Freqsnps = do.call(rbind, lapply(Freqsnps, data.frame)) |> 
  rownames_to_column("mrk") |> mutate(mrk = gsub('\\..*', '', mrk))
head(Freqsnps)
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

**Filtering step**

```{r echo=TRUE}
Freqall = apply(geno, 2, function(x){
  aux = as.data.frame(table(do.call(c, strsplit(x = x, split = ''))))
  return(aux)
})
Freqall = do.call(rbind, Freqall) |> 
  rownames_to_column("mrk") |> mutate(mrk = gsub('\\..*', '', mrk))
head(Freqall)
Freqmis = apply(geno, 2, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
head(Freqmis)
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

Removing markers with $\geq$ 5% of missing data

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = geno[,-which(Freqmis >= 0.05)]  
vcf@fix = vcf@fix[-which(Freqmis >= 0.05),]  
dim(geno)
any(is.na(geno))
```

. . .

[Impute missing data with the mode]{.red}

```{r echo=TRUE}
for (i in colnames(geno)) {
  if(!any(is.na(geno[,i]))) next else{
    geno[which(is.na(geno[,i])),i] = as.character(
      Freqsnps[which(Freqsnps$mrk == i), ][which.max(Freqsnps[which(Freqsnps$mrk == i), ][,'Freq']), "Var1"]
      )
  }
  rm(i)
}
any(is.na(geno))
```

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = geno[,-which(Freqall$Fper <= 0.05)]
```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol y = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol W \boldsymbol u + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

-   $\boldsymbol W \to$ matrix of markers recoded to numeric scale
-   $\boldsymbol u \to$ vector of marker effects 

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
RR-BLUP assumes that all markers effects are normally distributed and have identical variance:

$$
\boldsymbol u \sim \mathcal N \left(\boldsymbol 0, \sigma^2_u \boldsymbol I \right)
$$

:::

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol u \sim \mathcal N \left(\boldsymbol 0, \sigma^2_u \boldsymbol I \right)
$$

```{r echo=FALSE}
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = function(x) dnorm(x, 0, 1), colour = '#b2bc63', 
                linewidth = 1.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  xlim(-4,4) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(text = element_text(size = 18))
```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

Solution via mixed model equation

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol{1}^\prime \boldsymbol 1 & \boldsymbol 1^\prime \boldsymbol W \\
\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol 1 & \left(\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol W + \lambda \boldsymbol{I} \right)
\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol \mu \\
\boldsymbol u
\end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol 1^\prime \boldsymbol y \\
\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol y
\end{bmatrix}
$$

. . .

**Shrinkage factor**: Shrinks the marker effects towards zero

$$
\lambda = \frac{\sigma^2_\varepsilon}{\sigma^2_u}
$$

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

**Model parameters**

$$
\hat{\sigma}^2_g = \sigma^2_u \times t
$$

```{r echo=TRUE}
Vg = mod$Vu * ncol(geno_rr); Vg
```


```{r echo=TRUE}
Ve = mod$Ve; Ve
mu = mod$beta; mu
geno_her = Vg/(Vg + Ve); geno_her
cor(dat$blue, GEBV, use = "complete.obs")
```

## BayesB {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol y = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol W \boldsymbol u + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

-   $\boldsymbol W \to$ matrix of markers recoded to numeric scale
-   $\boldsymbol u \to$ vector of marker effects 

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
BayesB assumes that some markers are unimportant for the trait variation, hence have no effect. Furthermore, it relaxes the assumption that all markers have the same variance: 

$$
u_i \sim \mathcal N \left( 0, \sigma^2_{u_i} \right)
$$

:::

## BayesB {.custom1}

-   Prior for the variances: scaled inverse $\chi^2 \left[\sigma^2_{u_i} \sim \chi^{-2}\left(\nu\right)\right]$

. . .

-   Prior for the importance parameter (say, $I$): $I \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(\Pi)$

. . .

$$
\hat{g}_i = I_1 \times w_{1i} \times \hat u_1 + I_2 \times w_{2i} \times \hat u_2 + \dots + I_t \times w_{ti}  \times \hat u_t
$$

-   $I_j \to 1 \mbox{ or } 0$

## BayesB {.custom1}

Package `BGLR` [@perez_genome-wide_2014]

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(BGLR)
X_centred = scale(geno.code, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
ETA = list(list(X = X_centred, model = "BayesB")) ## This will determine the model
BayesB = BGLR(y = dat$blue, ETA = ETA, nIter = 80000, burnIn = 20000, 
              thin = 10, verbose = FALSE, saveAt = "Saves/dat/complete_")
```

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
X_centred = scale(geno.code, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
ETA = list(list(X = X_centred, model = "BayesB")) ## This will determine the model
load(file = "../Saves/RDA/bayesbmod.RData")
```

. . .

::::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.callout-caution style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
In [Bayesian models](https://github.com/storopoli/Estatistica-Bayesiana), you should mind the number of iterations, the burn-in phase and the thinning. The more, the better, but it will take longer for your model to run.
:::

## BayesB {.custom1}

**Convergence check through model diagnostics**: Package `coda` [@coda]

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.height=4}
library(coda)
varE = read.table("../Saves/dat/complete_varE.dat")[,1]
varE_chain = mcmc(varE[2001:length(varE)]) # burnIn/thin + 1
plot(varE_chain)
```

## BayesB {.custom1}

**Effective sample size**: The number of independent samples from posterior distributions. The higher, the better. If low, increase `nIter` or `thin`

```{r echo=TRUE}
effectiveSize(varE_chain)
```

. . .

**Geweke convergence test**: evaluates if the MCMC chain reached a stationary state. It should be between -1.96 and 1.96. If not, increase `burnIn`

```{r echo=TRUE}
geweke.diag(varE_chain)
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

**Define cross-validation parameters**

```{r echo=TRUE}
nfolds = 5
nrept = 5 
seed = 8  

sets = list()
i = 1
repeat{
  set.seed(987 * i)
  sets[[i]] = sample(rep(1:nfolds, length.out = nrow(dat)))
  i = i + 1
  if(i > nrept) break
}
cvdata = lapply(sets, function(x){
  cvdata = dat
  cvdata$set = x
  return(cvdata)
})
for (i in 1:length(cvdata)) cvdata[[i]]$rept = i

```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Run RRBLUP in cross-validation

```{r echo=TRUE}
cv_rr = lapply(cvdata, function(x){
  res.list = list()
  for (i in unique(x$set)) {
    
    yNA = x$blue
    yNA[x$set == i] = NA
    
    mod_cv = mixed.solve(y = yNA, Z = geno_rr)
    
    pred = c(mod_cv$beta) + (geno_rr %*% mod_cv$u)
    
    res.list[[i]] = cbind(
      x[x$set == i,],
      yhat = pred[x$set == i,]
    )
  }
  res.list
})
cv_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) do.call(rbind, x))
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Run BayesB in cross-validation

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
cv_bb = lapply(cvdata, function(x){
  res.list = list()
  for (i in unique(x$set)) {
    
    yNA = x$blue
    yNA[x$set == i] = NA
    
    mod_cv = BGLR(y = yNA, ETA = ETA, nIter = 8000, burnIn = 1000, 
                  thin = 10, verbose = FALSE, saveAt = "modCV")
    unlink(list.files(pattern = "modCV"))
    
    res.list[[i]] = data.frame(gen = x$gen, yhat = mod_cv$yHat) |> 
      left_join(x, by = "gen") |> filter(set == i)
  }
  res.list
})
cv_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) do.call(rbind, x))
```


```{r echo=FALSE}
load(file = "../Saves/RDA/cv_bb.RDA")
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Model evaluation

```{r echo=TRUE}
pa_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) cor(x$blue, x$yhat, use = 'complete.obs'))
mspe_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) sqrt(mean((x$blue - x$yhat)^2, na.rm = T)))

pa_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) cor(x$blue, x$yhat, use = 'complete.obs'))
mspe_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) sqrt(mean((x$blue - x$yhat)^2, na.rm = T)))
```


## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Model evaluation

```{r echo=TRUE}
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-height: 4.8

aux = data.frame(
  model = rep(c("RRBLUP", "BayesB"), each = nfolds*2),
  value = c(do.call(c, pa_rr), do.call(c, mspe_rr),
            do.call(c, pa_bb), do.call(c, mspe_bb)),
  param = c(rep(c("PA", "RMSPE"), each = 5), rep(c("PA", "RMSPE"), each = 5))
)

ggplot(data = aux, aes(x = model, y = value)) + 
  facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free_y") + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#b2bc63") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 18))+
  labs(x = "Model") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
```
